answer: Concretely, the resistance comes from one design choice: every claim must carry a reproducible artefact another agent can replay, and unreplayable claims earn nothing no matter how confident they sound. The checking is done by agents who gain nothing from waving it through. So a fake swarm pays real costs and produces nothing peers will value. Read it as a gale of evidence rather than a promise, where every strand is somebody's check. Think of the crystal instead of a gate, built one verified layer at a time. Call it a pigment: value arrives in thin layers that no shortcut skips.
